newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC LEADS SPANISH-BASED YUGOSLAVS INTO BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC LEADS SPANISH-BASED YUGOSLAVS INTO BATTLE.

text.p: Striker Predrag Mijatovic will lead a group of eight Spanish-based Yugoslavs into Saturday's vital World Cup qualifier against Spain in Valencia, the city where he made his name before moving to Real Madrid.
For Mijatovic the group six clash is the latest chapter in a tumultuous December.

Just ten days ago he saw his young son rushed to hospital for an emergency operation. Three days later he led Real to victory over arch-rivals Barcelona, and now the striker will encounter not only his former fans in the Mediterranean city, but also some of his current team mates.

But one man Mijatovic will be happy not to see on Saturday is Real Madrid midfielder Fernando Hierro, who limped off the field towards the end of the match against Barcelona with the knee injury and is still injured.
"It's an important loss for the Spanish side," Mijatovic said.
Josep Guardiola, on the losing side in the Real-Barcelona clash, is likely to replace Hierro, who plays as a link man between defence and midfield.

Mijatovic's likely duel with friend and team mate Rafael Alkorta will be echoed by personal battles between Atletico Madrid's Kiko Narvaez and Milinko Pantic, and Deportivo Coruna's Miroslav Djukic and Javier Manjarin.

Other Spanish-based players in the Yugoslav line-up include defender Hristo Vidakovic, who warmed up with a spectacular individual goal for Real Betis last weekend, and Darko Kovacevic, who has shot to prominence at Real Sociedad.
Kovacevic may take over as Mijatovic's strike partner in place of Aston Villa's Savo Milosevic, who scored a hat-trick in Yugoslavia's 8-1 win in the Faroe Islands.

Betis's Albert Nadj, Tenerife's Slavisa Jokanovic and Branko Brnovic of Espanyol make up the rest of the Spanish contingent in a Yugoslav squad cobbled together from players from seven different leagues.
Even the president of the Yugoslav Football Federation, Miljan Miljanic used to be at Real Madrid and still speaks good Spanish.
Spain-Yugoslavia clashes have produced some classic games, amongst them Spain's 1-0 victory in Belgrade which earned the country a place in the 1978 World Cup Finals.

Yugoslavia took revenge by knocking the Spaniards out of the 1990 competition in Italy. The scorer of both Yugoslav goals in that game, Dragan Stojkovic, who now plays in Japan, is now captain of the side.
"I'm a friend of (Spanish goalkeeper Andoni) Zubizarreta, and I hope he remembers me," Stojkovic said.

The subsequent Yugoslav ban from international competition and the dispersion of its leading players means that the national side lacks match practice, so heavy rain in Spain this week which disrupted training sessions came as a blow to manager Slobodan Santrac.
"We have lacked time to harmonise the flow of the players," he said.
The showers are likely to continue and the pitch at the Mestalla stadium could cut up badly during the game.

For Javier Clemente the weather has not been the problem in the build-up to Saturday's clash. The dour Spanish manager has been more concerned by what he viewed as excessive coverage of the Real-Barcelona clash last Saturday.
"This game's 5,000 times more important than that one," he growled.
Teams:
Spain - Andoni Zubizarreta, Alberto Belsue, Rafael Alkorta, Abelardo Fernandez, Sergi Barjuan, Josep Guardiola, Julen Guerrero, Luis Enrique Martinez, Raul Gonzalez, Juan Pizzi, Kiko Narvaez.

Yugoslavia (from) - Kocic Aleksandar, Zvonko Milojevic, Hristo Vidakovic, Bratislav Zivkovic, Nisa Savlejic, Miroslav Djukic, Goran Djorovic, Dragan Stojkovic, Branko Brnovic, Dejan Govedarica, Sasa Curcic, Slavisa Jokanovic, Vladimir Jugovic, Milinko Pantic, Albert Nadj, Predrag Mijatovic, Dejan Savicevic, Savo Milosevic, Darko Kovacevic, Anto Drobnjak
